clue.text: Hoo-has resulting from the rise of pop…

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads the word upwards, so pop's synonym is taken from the bottom

parts.note: pop is a fizzy soft drink, soda

explanation.surface: Fusses kicked up by pop music getting popular, a lead-in to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoo-has are commotions or fusses, and 'ados' are fusses too, as in much ado.

clue.text: …it's music marketed at teens primarily, occasionally hurried and juvenile

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of each of the five words before it
occasionally means taking only every other letter of the word hurried

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: pop is music sold to teenagers, rushed out and childish.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 1 Down so the two read as one sentence about pop music; 'occasionally' here means every other letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Juvenile and immature are synonyms for childish, lacking adult development.

clue.text: Single — the first from Revolver — is something unlike anything else

parts.note: single means one

indicators.note: the first from asks for the opening letter of the album title Revolver

explanation.surface: A single from the Beatles album Revolver is one of a kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A oner is British slang for a unique person or thing, one that has no equal.

clue.text: Wild Rolling Stone with a lager!

indicators.note: rolling suggests tumbling over, so the letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A Rolling Stone, beer in hand, running riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling Stone' reads as the band, but 'Rolling' is the anagram signal working on ST plus A LAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrestal is a botanical term for plants growing wild among crops, uncultivated weeds.

clue.text: A pop singer is quick to follow fashion, we're told

indicators.note: to follow puts the word for quick after the other piece
we're told signals that a word is heard rather than read, so its spelling changes

parts.note: to fashion something is to make or tailor it
quick means swift

explanation.surface: A pop star is said to be quick to pick up the latest trends.
explanation.definitionFit: Taylor Swift is one of the world's best-selling pop singers.

clue.text: Plaintive intro to requiem fuels more tears

indicators.note: intro to asks for the opening letter of the word requiem
tears as a verb means rips apart, so the letters are torn into a new order

explanation.surface: The opening of a requiem makes a mourner weep even more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' reads as crying, but is the verb 'rips', rearranging FUELS MORE into EMORSEFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaintive and remorseful both describe a sorrowful, regretful, mournful tone.

clue.text: Eccentric singer knocking back a second drink with conviction

indicators.note: knocking back, like downing a drink, turns the run of words before it backwards

parts.note: MO is short for moment, a second
to lap is to drink, as a cat does
conviction means firm belief, faith

explanation.surface: An odd vocalist downs a second drink with real certainty.
explanation.definitionFit: Paloma Faith is an English singer known for her flamboyant, quirky style.

clue.text: Lyric poems found in the cases of old elegists

indicators.note: the cases of a word are its outside letters, here of old and of elegists

explanation.surface: Lyric verse turns up among the works of ancient elegy writers.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyric poems addressed to a subject, often in elevated style.

clue.text: Rock band with a normal lead singer

indicators.note: to rock is to shake, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A rock group with an ordinary frontman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock band' reads as a genre, but 'Rock' is the anagram signal and 'band' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Damon Albarn is the frontman of Blur and Gorillaz, a band's main vocalist.

clue.text: Musician's house is wicked and large, with lavish surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings says the word for lavish goes around the other pieces

parts.note: lavish means grand, splendid
wicked is slang for excellent, ace
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A star's home described as fabulous, big and opulently set.
explanation.definitionFit: Graceland is Elvis Presley's mansion in Memphis, a musician's home.

clue.text: The place to see Steps supporting Another Level?

definitions.text: The place to see Steps supporting Another Level?

parts.words: The place to see Steps supporting Another Level?
parts.note: Steps and Another Level were both 1990s pop groups; read literally, a flight of steps holding up the next floor is found in this shaft

explanation.surface: Where to catch the band Steps opening for the boy band Another Level.
explanation.definitionFit: A stairwell is the vertical space housing a staircase, where steps rise to each floor.

clue.text: Nothing fits in-between a lot of very large instruments

indicators.note: fits in-between says one piece is slotted into the middle of the other
a lot of means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: very large means obese
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Nothing fits between a lot of very large instruments, as if squeezed in an orchestra pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Oboes are double-reed woodwind instruments of the orchestra.

clue.text: The noise coming from an elephant's backside, outwardly offensive

definitions.text: The noise coming from an elephant's

indicators.note: outwardly says the word for offensive sits on the outside, around the other piece

parts.note: the Tet Offensive was the 1968 Vietnam War campaign, so offensive can suggest Tet
backside means rump

explanation.surface: A rude noise from the rear end of an elephant.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests flatulence; the definition is the elephant's call, with 's read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An elephant's loud call is named after the brass instrument, a blare from its trunk.

clue.text: Orchestral arrangements featuring some joyful notes

indicators.note: featuring some says only part of the run of letters across these two words is used

explanation.surface: Orchestrations including a few cheerful notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tra-la is a sung refrain of carefree notes, a nonsense expression of gaiety.

clue.text: Transporting small piano with a courier is risky

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

indicators.note: transporting means carrying off, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Moving a little piano with a delivery firm is a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' gives S, which ends up at the very end, outside the rearranged P plus A COURIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Precarious means unsafe or likely to fall, so risky.

clue.text: After break time, put on another concert

indicators.note: after says the word for time comes behind the word for break

parts.note: a break is a rest
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: After an interval, a band plays a second show.
explanation.definitionFit: To restage is to mount a performance again, a repeat production.

clue.text: Very early cover of record initially had Orbison's disapproval

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the three following words

explanation.surface: An early record sleeve drew Roy Orbison's disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very early cover' reads as a record sleeve, but means an ancient garment.
explanation.definitionFit: An ephod is a vestment worn by priests in ancient Israel, a garment from biblical times.

clue.text: Singer led drunkenly into A&E

indicators.note: into says the rearranged letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: the letters A and E, as in a hospital's accident and emergency department

indicators.note: drunkenly says the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A singer is taken, tipsy, into the emergency department.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British hospital accident and emergency department; 'drunkenly' rearranges LED as DEL before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Adele is a best-selling British vocalist.

clue.text: Album sleeves are going round

indicators.note: sleeves is a verb here: the record's letters encase the other piece as a sleeve holds a disc

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record, an album
A is the abbreviation for are, a metric unit of area

explanation.surface: Record covers revolving on a turntable.
explanation.definitionFit: A lap is one circuit of a track, a single trip round.

clue.text: After mini-album is rejected and scrapped, have a go at focusing on the technical details

indicators.note: after puts the attempt at the end, behind the other pieces
rejected means thrown back, so the record's letters are reversed

parts.note: an EP, extended play, is a short album

indicators.note: scrapped suggests broken up, so the letters of and are rearranged

parts.note: to have a go at something is to try it

explanation.surface: After a short record is dropped and binned, a musician tries again, fussing over every detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is rejected' reverses EP to PE; 'scrapped' rearranges AND to DAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantry is excessive concern with minor points and rules, fussiness over fine points.

clue.text: See 7
Imminent release from Phil Collins — out tonight!

indicators.note: out says the last word is dropped from the song title

parts.note: In the Air Tonight is Phil Collins's 1981 hit single

explanation.surface: A trailer for a new Phil Collins single, on sale tonight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in the air is about to happen, felt to be coming soon.

clue.text: Hard 80s pop star

definitions.meaning: hard as in unyielding, refusing to be moved
... fronted Adam and the Ants, a British new-wave act of the early 1980s

explanation.surface: A tough star of 1980s pop.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means unbending or hard, and Adam Ant was a chart-topping 80s singer.

clue.text: See 9
Begin to like the sound of a second recording

indicators.note: the sound of says the phrase is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a second recording in a studio is take two

explanation.surface: Starting to warm to how a second take sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To take to someone or something is to start liking them, to warm to them.

clue.text: Allowed record boxes to be removed

indicators.note: boxes is a verb here: the record's letters enclose the other piece

parts.note: a deed is a legal record
allowed means let

explanation.surface: A record is allowed to be withdrawn from sale, its boxed sets cleared.
explanation.definitionFit: Deleted means struck out or erased, so taken away.

clue.text: Make a recording with leads from audio input port

parts.note: to dub is to copy a recording

indicators.note: leads from takes the opening letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: Recording using the cables from an audio input socket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like a socket in the surface, but is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is a major Gulf seaport and city in the United Arab Emirates.

clue.text: Unable to hear sound fade out

indicators.note: out means wrong or off, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Can't hear the music fading away.
explanation.definitionFit: Deaf means lacking the power of hearing.

clue.text: Rapper from Kenya blowing up with extraordinary set

indicators.note: blowing up means exploding, so the letters are scattered into a new order
extraordinary says the letters are put out of their ordinary order

explanation.surface: A rapper from Kenya becomes a star with an amazing set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing up' turns KENYA into KANYE; 'extraordinary' turns SET into EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Kanye West is an American hip-hop artist and producer.

clue.text: Disco biscuits reportedly alleviate pain

indicators.note: reportedly says the slang term is heard rather than read

parts.note: disco biscuits is club slang for ecstasy tablets, known as Es

explanation.surface: Pills at a disco said to relieve suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease pain is to lessen it, to make suffering more bearable.

clue.text: Songbirds being somewhat dulcet, it seems

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Little birds sound rather sweet, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'Songbirds being' took in 'being', which is only a link word joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tits are small songbirds, such as blue tits and great tits.

clue.text: An unreal performance by Strummer?

parts.note: Joe Strummer of the Clash was a guitarist, but here a strummer mimes playing an imaginary instrument

explanation.surface: A fake show by Joe Strummer, the Clash frontman.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing this is miming strumming chords with no instrument at all, an imaginary performance.
